notes: §1985:IX.4.4.4 GR7: "If label records are specified for the file, the beginning labels are processed as follows": for INPUT "the execution of the OPEN statement causes the labels to be checked in accordance with the implementor's specified conventions for input label checking", for OUTPUT they are written by the output convention, and "The behavior of the OPEN statement when label records are specified but not present, or when label records are not specified but are present, is undefined." The processing is implementor-defined (§1985:C.2 item 61 names this rule: "The labels are checked or written in accordance with the implementor's specified conventions for input or output label handling"). The implementation's convention is that a file carries no label the COBOL program can see: labels belong to the host file system (§1985:C.1: "Specifying the presence of file labels is considered a function of the operating system and as such does not belong in the COBOL program"), and docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md Table 7 row 7.4 states it as 'accepted-inert at 85'. The clause is parsed at 85 (FileDescriptionFormats.Rows admits it in every FD format; VersionConformancePass.VisitLabelRecordsClause refuses it from 2002, COBOL0902) and no binder or runtime member reads it, so the INPUT and OUTPUT arms of KeyedConnector.OpenCore check and write no label, which is the whole of the convention; the rule's last sentence leaves the mismatch cases undefined, so they carry no obligation. Probed at --std 85: a file written under LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD is read back under LABEL RECORD IS OMITTED and under no clause with status 00 and the same records. The witness writes and reads back a LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD indexed file. Not covered by this verdict: the clause's own syntax is unchecked at 85 (kb/Work PB5070), and docs/CONFORMANCE.md has no entry for the 1985 implementor-defined list's label items (§1985:C.2 items 60 and 61), so the convention is written down only in the VCR row.

next.reason: 1985: "If label records are specified for the file, the beginning labels are processed as follows"; 2023: "No OPEN general rule (14.9.27.4) mentions labels or label checking/writing; the label records feature is not carried". The 2023 OPEN general rules cover the statement in full but say nothing of beginning label checking or writing, nor of undefined results for missing or unexpected labels.
